Snake.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes a Snake instance by setting its length and score to fixed defaults, caching all four constructor parameters as instance attributes, and computing the snake's starting position as the floating-point center of the screen." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> SCREEN_WIDTH </REF>: numeric "Width of the game screen in pixels; used both to cache as an instance attribute and to compute the initial horizontal center position"
        <REF> SCREEN_HEIGHT </REF>: numeric "Height of the game screen in pixels; used both to cache as an instance attribute and to compute the initial vertical center position"
        <REF> BLOCK_SIZE </REF>: numeric "Size of one grid block in pixels; cached as an instance attribute but not used in any computation within this method"
        <REF> food_position </REF>: any "Initial position of the food item; cached as an instance attribute but not used in any computation within this method"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Set self.length to the integer literal 1 RESULT self.length]
            [COMMAND Set self.score to the integer literal 0 RESULT self.score]
            [COMMAND Set self.SCREEN_WIDTH to the value of the SCREEN_WIDTH parameter RESULT self.SCREEN_WIDTH]
            [COMMAND Set self.SCREEN_HEIGHT to the value of the SCREEN_HEIGHT parameter RESULT self.SCREEN_HEIGHT]
            [COMMAND Set self.BLOCK_SIZE to the value of the BLOCK_SIZE parameter RESULT self.BLOCK_SIZE]
            [COMMAND Compute the horizontal center as SCREEN_WIDTH divided by 2 using true division (result is float) and the vertical center as SCREEN_HEIGHT divided by 2 using true division (result is float); construct a single-element list containing one tuple of those two float values and assign it to self.positions RESULT self.positions]
            [COMMAND Set self.food_position to the value of the food_position parameter RESULT self.food_position]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Snake.move:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Updates the snake's head position by advancing one grid cell in the given direction with screen-wrapping, then either resets the game on self-collision, eats food if the new position matches it, or slides the body forward by prepending the new head and trimming the tail to maintain the snake's current length." move]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> direction </REF>: tuple(int, int) "A 2-tuple (x, y) encoding the movement vector for one step, e.g. (1,0) for right, (0,-1) for up"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Read self.positions[0] into cur, representing the current head position as a (x, y) tuple RESULT cur]
            [COMMAND Unpack direction into scalar components x and y RESULT x, y]
            [COMMAND Compute new head position: new_x = (cur[0] + x * self.BLOCK_SIZE) % self.SCREEN_WIDTH and new_y = (cur[1] + y * self.BLOCK_SIZE) % self.SCREEN_HEIGHT, assembling both into a 2-tuple; the modulo ensures wrapping at screen boundaries in both axes and always yields a valid on-screen grid coordinate RESULT new]
            [COMMAND If new equals self.food_position, call self.eat_food() RESULT food_check]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the collision guard: check len(self.positions) > 2 (short-circuit guard, skips membership test when the list has 2 or fewer elements) AND new in self.positions[2:] (new head lands on a body segment beyond the neck) RESULT collision]
            [COMMAND If collision is true, call self.reset() to restart the game; execution of the move ends here for this branch RESULT reset_result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise (collision is false), insert new at index 0 of self.positions, making it the new head RESULT positions_after_insert]
            [COMMAND If len(self.positions) strictly exceeds self.length after the insert, call self.positions.pop() to remove the last (tail) element, keeping the list exactly self.length entries long RESULT positions_after_trim]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: new equals self.food_position before the collision check]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call self.eat_food() to handle food consumption; execution then continues to the collision check without returning early RESULT eat_food_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: len(self.positions) is 2 or fewer, making positions[2:] an empty slice]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND The short-circuit in the collision condition (len > 2) evaluates to false immediately, so the membership test is skipped entirely and the else branch (normal movement) is always taken RESULT short_circuit_skip]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: After inserting new, len(self.positions) does not exceed self.length]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the pop() call; the positions list grows by one, which happens when the snake has eaten food and its length has increased RESULT no_trim]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Snake.random_food_position:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Repeatedly generates a random grid-aligned (x, y) coordinate for food placement until the chosen position does not coincide with any of the snake's current body segment positions." random_food_position]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The game instance, providing food_position (current food coordinate tuple), positions (collection of occupied grid coordinates representing the snake body), SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHT, and BLOCK_SIZE constants"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether self.food_position is a member of self.positions; if it is not, skip the loop body entirely and return without changes RESULT loop_condition_initial]
            [COMMAND While self.food_position is contained in self.positions, generate a new candidate x-coordinate by drawing a random integer in the inclusive range [0, SCREEN_WIDTH // BLOCK_SIZE - 1] and multiplying by BLOCK_SIZE to snap to a valid grid column RESULT candidate_x]
            [COMMAND Within the same loop iteration, generate a new candidate y-coordinate by drawing a random integer in the inclusive range [0, SCREEN_HEIGHT // BLOCK_SIZE - 1] and multiplying by BLOCK_SIZE to snap to a valid grid row RESULT candidate_y]
            [COMMAND Assign the tuple (candidate_x, candidate_y) to self.food_position, replacing the previous candidate RESULT self.food_position]
            [COMMAND Re-evaluate the loop condition; repeat the three steps above if the new self.food_position is still contained in self.positions, otherwise exit the loop RESULT loop_exit]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: self.food_position is not in self.positions before the first iteration]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the loop body entirely; self.food_position remains unchanged and the method returns immediately RESULT no_op]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Snake.reset:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Resets the snake's state to its initial values by setting length to 1, centering the starting position on screen, zeroing the score, and placing food at a new random location." reset]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Set self.length to the scalar integer 1, establishing the minimum entity size RESULT self.length]
            [COMMAND Set self.positions to a single-element list containing one tuple; compute the x-coordinate as self.SCREEN_WIDTH divided by 2 and the y-coordinate as self.SCREEN_HEIGHT divided by 2, placing the head at the center of the screen RESULT self.positions]
            [COMMAND Set self.score to the scalar integer 0, resetting the accumulator to its baseline value RESULT self.score]
            [COMMAND Call self.random_food_position() to place food at a new random location on the board RESULT food_position_side_effect]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Snake.eat_food:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Increases the snake's length by 1 and score by 100, then repositions the food at a new random location on the board." eat_food]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Increment self.length by 1 RESULT self.length]
            [COMMAND Increment self.score by 100 RESULT self.score]
            [COMMAND Call self.random_food_position() to place food at a new random position RESULT food_position]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
